targets.title: Standing enhances cognitive control and alters visual search
targets.evidence_quote: The primary goal of this paper was to replicate the effect of posture (sit vs. stand) on cognitive performance obtained by Smith et al. (2019) across their three attention paradigms: a Stroop task, a task-switching paradigm, and a visual search task.
targets.outcome_quote: Upon closely replicating these three experiments, we consistently failed to observe the key findings of interest. That is, we were unable to obtain meaningful effects of posture on the magnitude of the Stroop effect in Experiment 1, on switch costs in Experiment 2, or on the search rate in Experiment 3.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly give an overall failed verdict across the three replications. A small error-rate result is judged not meaningful by the authors. Rosenbaum et al. and other replications are background rather than the closest retested paper in the chain.
